summary.text: A 52-year-old man presented with bilateral blurred vision and photophobia that had progressively worsened over a few weeks. He had acute myeloid leukemia with an FLT3-ITD mutation, diagnosed four years earlier and initially treated with cytarabine and allogeneic stem cell transplantation, relapsed 18 months after transplant, and then received Gilteritinib 120 mg/day for two years.

Best-corrected acuity was 20/100 right and 20/40 left. Slit-lamp examination showed punctate epithelial staining, persistent epithelial defects with rolled edges in both eyes and right stromal opacity. Corneal sensation was reduced, 10 mm right and 15 mm left, while eyelids, tear breakup time and Schirmer test were normal and no infection or anterior chamber inflammation was seen. He was diagnosed with bilateral stage 2 neurotrophic keratitis.

Topical insulin with preservative-free artificial tears was started and Gilteritinib was discontinued with the hematologists. At one week the punctate epitheliopathy had resolved and the defects had healed, and topical insulin and lubricants were continued. At one month acuity was 20/32 right and 20/20 left, with a central corneal leukoma over about half of the pupillary area.
